text: Lives in a room with a desk and a keyboard.
Just a guy who keeps going back to the thing he likes.
Tuesday the keyboard was just a keyboard.
Cairn walked in because he felt like it.
He played until it got dark.
Didn't owe the chair a full hour.
Left when the song was done.
Wrote KEYS on it like it was standup.
Even put the room in the invite like someone else was coming.
Like, okay, I'm not flaking on this anymore.
Wednesday he checked the square twice.
Wednesday night he walked past the keyboard and didn't touch it.
Cairn sits down like it's a meeting.
He plays the whole hour anyway because the calendar said so.
He stands up like the call is over.
Friday morning he walks past the desk and feels guilty.
Keyboard's just sitting there looking at him.
Like a task he didn't finish.
Used to walk over and want it.
Now he walks over and it's homework.
Puts his mug down and leaves so he doesn't owe it another minute.
Someone on a writing board said it.
What's a passion will turn into a chore.
An artist said they booked an hour to be creative and then sat there in nothing.
Another person said they feel guilty every time they see the keyboard.
He didn't fall off the thing.
He put it on the calendar like work.
People who study this gave it a boring name.
They had people put a clock time on stuff that used to be free.
Once it had a start time, it felt like a job.
The fun didn't leave the thing.
The fun left when the block showed up.
So he does the small thing.
He doesn't make a better standup.
Doesn't set a reminder to be inspired.
If he wants the keyboard, he walks over.
If he doesn't, he walks past.
He doesn't owe it an hour.
Later he walks over at four.
Plays one song because he's already there.
He booked it like a standup.
